summary: Discovery call to understand NaviPort's integration needs for conversational indexing/search and document embeddings. Main drivers: predictable latency for customer-facing assistants, cost controls, and ability to run in a VPC/on-prem for regulated customers. Discussed SDK options, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy model, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Redwood to run benchmarks and provide pricing + security docs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-05-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (NaviPort CTO), Aisha (Dir Platform), Liam (SRE), Sofia (PM)

[00:00:05] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Jordan, account lead, and Priya is our SE who will dig into the technical pieces. how about you all?
[00:00:18] Carlos (NaviPort): yeah I'm Carlos, CT O. we run the platform and own the inference stack decisions. Aisha will speak more on platform requirements.
[00:00:25] Aisha: hi all, thanks — our main objective is to add an assistant experience to our portal and a search layer for internal docs. need to understand integration work and what hosting options look like.
[00:00:40] Priya (Redwood): great. can I ask a couple quick qualifiers? what's your expected qps and latency SLO, and are you leaning hosted/dedicated/private today?
[00:00:52] Carlos: we have two classes of traffic — internal tooling calls ~50 qps, and customer-facing chat that's bursty — peak up to 120 qps. latency target is p95 under 350ms for the chat path.
[00:01:08] Liam (NaviPort): also important — some customers require their data never leave their VPC, so private option may be necessary for those accounts.
[00:01:16] Jordan: noted. that p95 target helps. Redwood supports hosted for quick start, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private/VPC packages for full isolation. Priya — can you talk SDK surface and adapters?
[00:01:30] Priya: sure. we have official SDKs for Python and Node with streaming, function calling, and embeddings endpoints. we also maintain plug-and-play adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. typically for a search/assistant flow we'd recommend using the SDK's batch embedding route and the SDK + LangChain connector for orchestration.
[00:01:56] Carlos: that's good. we use LangChain already in our orchestration layer. is there an adapter for LlamaIndex as well?
[00:02:04] Priya: yes, we provide an LlamaIndex connector — small wrapper that maps the index calls to Redwood's embedding APIs and allows prefix caching. a couple caveats: LlamaIndex wants synchronous calls, so for higher throughput we recommend the SDK's async batch endpoints or using our gateway to manage multiplexing.
[00:02:25] Sofia (NaviPort): can you explain the gateway option? we have an Envoy sidecar pattern today.
[00:02:31] Priya: absolutely. our gateway is a lightweight proxy that sits in front of your network, or you can run a sidecar. it handles rate limiting, routing to hosted/dedicated/private backends, token-aware batching, and observability hooks. think of it like a policy plane + efficient request router.
[00:02:52] Aisha: would that mean we don't have to change existing LangChain calls?
[00:02:58] Priya: often minimal changes — the gateway can present the same HTTP surface as the SDK in many cases; for deep integrations you might use the SDK directly. the gateway is useful for centralized quotas and consistent telemetry across teams.
[00:03:12] [00:03:15] Liam: what about KV cache and prefix caching — we have a lot of repeated system prompts and doc contexts.
[00:03:21] Priya: we support prefix/KV cache at the gateway level and in the runtime. caching reduces cost and latency by maintaining token caches for active sessions. small note: in some transcripts the engine shows K V cash spelled weirdly in logs but logic remains the same — apologies for the transcription glitch.
[00:03:42] Carlos: laugh — noted. on quotas: we need per-team quotas and the ability to throttle per-customer. how granular do your rate policies get?
[00:03:50] Jordan: quite granular — per-api-key, per-team, per-route quotas, burst windows, and token-based throttling. we expose management APIs so platform teams can programmatically adjust quotas.
[00:04:03] Aisha: do you support hierarchical quotas? e.g., org limit and child team limits?
[00:04:09] Priya: yes we do. you can set org-wide caps and then allocate per-team pools. there's also automatic fallbacks to cheaper/compatible model variants if a pool is exhausted.
[00:04:20] Sofia: can the fallback be disabled for specific flows? we have regulated flows that must not change model outputs.
[00:04:26] Priya: absolutely — you can pin routes to a model version and disable fallback or set strict failover behaviors.
[00:04:33] [00:04:40] Carlos: security stuff — SOC2 and KMS integrations, SSO?
[00:04:45] Jordan: we provide SOC2 Type II reports and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for keys in Private deployments. SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC are supported in Console for Dedicated/Private. we'll send the SOC2 and VPC onboarding doc after the call.
[00:04:59] Liam: for Private deployments, how much operational work falls on our side vs Redwood?
[00:05:05] Priya: private is shipped as a customer-managed control plane with Redwood providing an installer and an opinionated runtime. typical model: Redwood supports install, upgrades, and critical issues; the customer's infra team operates day-to-day networking and hosts. we also offer a managed on-prem tier if you want us to handle more of the ops.
[00:05:26] Carlos: what about observability? we need traces correlated to our request ids and token-level cost breakdown per request.
[00:05:33] Priya: we export structured telemetry: per-request traces, token counts, model and route metadata, latency buckets and flamegraphs where needed. integrations include Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and logs to your ELK/Datadog. we also provide per-token cost attributes so you can attribute spend to product features.
[00:05:53] [00:06:00] Aisha: great — and can we instrument our existing dashboards?
[00:06:03] Jordan: yes, many customers pipe telemetry to their existing stacks. we can send sample dashboards and queries for Datadog/Prometheus.
[00:06:12] Sofia: on SDKs: is there a hosted key rotation mechanism and short-lived tokens for edge clients?
[00:06:18] Priya: yep — short-lived signed tokens for browser/edge usage, and key rotation APIs for server keys. private deployments can use your KMS for signing.
[00:06:27] [00:06:35] Carlos: performance — could you run a benchmark with our prompts and target p95 350ms?
[00:06:41] Priya: yes, we'll need sample payloads, prompt length distributions, and expected concurrency. we'll run hosted and dedicated configs. Jordan: we'll propose a test matrix and timeline right after this.
[00:06:54] Liam: curious about batch vs streaming — we plan to stream partial results to users. how does batching affect streaming latency?
[00:07:02] Priya: good call. streaming is compatible with our runtime. we do smart batching: for streaming flows we use micro-batches to preserve token-by-token streaming while gaining some batching efficiency. there's a tradeoff window (usually 10-30ms) but you keep a streaming experience.
[00:07:20] Carlos: any gotchas with LangChain memory layers and the gateway?
[00:07:25] Priya: memory layers that rely on synchronous, per-call embedding generation might see latency; we recommend async batch endpoints during ingestion. for runtime memory reads we use cached embeddings or KV cache at the gateway to avoid repeated NN calls.
[00:07:41] [00:07:55] Aisha: SLA question — what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[00:07:59] Jordan: Dedicated includes an SLA for uptime and P99 latency targets by contract. we'll surface specific numbers in the SLA doc; typical commitments are 99.9% uptime and defined latency tiers per model family.
[00:08:12] Sofia: cost — we're sensitive; can you outline cost controls?
[00:08:17] Priya: main levers are batching policies, prefix caching, quantization profiles for models, route-based model selection (cheaper variant for non-prod), and quota enforcement. Redwood Optimize can make suggestions from workload traces.
[00:08:31] Carlos: we may need on-prem for some regulated customers. if we go private, can we still use Redwood Console?
[00:08:37] Priya: for private we provide an on-prem console or a hybrid where the control plane is customer-managed and we surface telemetry to your instance. remote Console access can be restricted via network controls.
[00:08:50] [00:09:10] Jordan: quick qualification — timeline? when would you like to start a pilot?
[00:09:14] Carlos: target Q3 for pilot with a small set of customers. internal timeline to decide ~4–6 weeks.
[00:09:24] Jordan: ok that's reasonable. success criteria?
[00:09:27] Sofia: for pilot: p95 <350ms for chat, embedding ingestion under 10s/1000 docs, observability hooks in our dashboards, and clear cost estimates.
[00:09:40] Priya: good list — we'll map the benchmark metrics to those criteria.
[00:09:45] [00:10:02] Carlos: integration effort — do you have examples of customers that used Envoy sidecar vs standalone gateway?
[00:10:09] Priya: yes — a few fintechs ran Envoy sidecars to fit into their mesh; others used our gateway as a central proxy on the VPC egress. sidecar pattern reduces network hop changes but requires per-service deployment; central gateway simplifies ops but adds a routing hop. we can share case studies.
[00:10:30] Aisha: cross-team ownership — who will maintain quota configs? platform team or product teams?
[00:10:35] Jordan: typically platform owns org-level quotas and exposes self-serve tooling for product teams to request increases.
[00:10:42] [00:11:10] Liam: developer experience — how quickly can devs swap SDK calls for the gateway? any code samples?
[00:11:17] Priya: code samples in our repo — swapping endpoint URL and auth header gets you a long way. for streaming there's a small change in client-side websockets or SSE usage but we provide examples for both Python and Node.
[00:11:30] Sofia: can we do a short pilot just with embeddings first? that's lower risk.
[00:11:34] Jordan: yes many customers start with embeddings and then expand into chat. we'll scope the pilot to embeddings ingestion + retrieval + basic chat route.
[00:11:44] [00:12:00] Carlos: any regulatory support for EU data residency?
[00:12:05] Priya: hosted has region controls; for strict residency you'd pick Dedicated in the EU region or Private deployment in your data center.
[00:12:15] Aisha: storage retention and purge APIs?
[00:12:18] Jordan: yes retention policies and deletion APIs are available; for Private you can configure retention to match compliance rules.
[00:12:29] [00:13:05] Priya: ok next is the technical path — we'll request a prompt corpus, throughput profile, and decide test matrix: hosted baseline, dedicated with reserved pool, private install demo. we'll test p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost per request, and failure modes under quota exhaustion.
[00:13:25] Carlos: do you emulate network egress constraints for on-prem?
[00:13:29] Priya: yes, in private we test under realistic networking and VPC NAT conditions.
[00:13:36] [00:13:50] Jordan: I'll send the initial pilot statement of work + pricing options. any blocker items we didn't surface?
[00:13:57] Sofia: just one — our legal team will want to review data handling in hosted mode; we'll need contract markups.
[00:14:05] Jordan: understood — Jordan will include standard contract language and where redlines typically occur.
[00:14:12] [00:14:25] Aisha: timeline for benchmark results?
[00:14:28] Priya: with samples in hand we can run the hosted vs dedicated runs in about 3 business days and deliver a results doc plus recommendations.
[00:14:36] Carlos: great.
[00:14:40] [00:32:00] [note: call had a quiet period where participants reviewed docs, some cross talk omitted]
[00:32:15] Priya: sharing a quick anecdote — one customer reduced token spend by ~38% by enabling prefix cache on repeated system messages and switching to a quantized model for background batch jobs.
[00:32:30] Aisha: that's compelling.
[00:32:45] Carlos: last technical Q — model variant compatibility matrix? we onboard open models and also provide guidance on quantization tradeoffs.
[00:32:52] Priya: yes we maintain a compatibility matrix that lists supported topologies (attn variants, kv cache behavior) and recommended quantization profiles per model. will include it in the follow-up.
[00:33:10] [00:40:00] Jordan: quick recap and next steps: we'll send pilot SOW + pricing, Priya runs benchmarks with provided prompt set, security docs and SOC2 will be shared, and then we schedule the SE-deep dive once benchmarks are in.
[00:40:20] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:40:30] Aisha: thanks, looking forward.
[00:40:35] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up by Friday. bye.
[00:40:40] [call ends]

Notes on transcription artifacts: some speaker labels intermittently show first name only; occasional mis-heard terms (K V cash) and model names aliased (e.g., Redwood Dedicatedy) appear in the transcript — cleaned where obvious but left original phrasing in places to preserve verbatim feel.
